subject: general
question: What percentage of jobs in India are at risk of automation, as per World Bank data, 2016?
solution:
The correct answer is __**69%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The World Bank data** from **2016** suggests that around **69% of jobs in India** are** susceptible to automation.**
 
• This means that the tasks currently performed by individuals in these jobs could potentially be automated by **machines, artificial intelligence, or other technological advancements** in the future.
 
• **Automation **has the potential to significantly alter the employment landscape by replacing certain types of jobs with automated processes, leading to changes in job requirements, skill sets, and employment opportunities.
 
• It is important for policymakers, businesses, and individuals to understand the implications of automation on the labor market and to develop strategies to adapt to these changes effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The World Bank **is an international financial institution focused on providing financial assistance to the governments of low- and middle-income countries for capital projects.
 
• It consists of two main entities: the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and the International Development Association (IDA).
 
• These entities offer loans and grants to support various development initiatives, including infrastructure projects, poverty reduction efforts, and economic reforms.
 
• The World Bank was established in 1944, alongside the International Monetary Fund (IMF), during the Bretton Woods Conference.
